Reading Analogue Clocks:
🕰️ Reading Analogue Clocks 🕰️

Learning the language of the big and little hands!

1. The Two Main Hands

An analogue clock shows time using hands moving around a circle! The short hand moves slowly and points to the Hour. The long hand moves faster and points to the Minutes!

2. Reading the Minutes

The numbers on the clock face (1 to 12) are a secret code for the minute hand! You have to count by 5s. If the long hand points to the 1, it means 5 minutes. If it points to the 3, it means 15 minutes! If it points straight up at the 12, it means exactly 00 minutes (on the hour).

3. Half and Quarter Hours

  • When the minute hand points to 3, it is Quarter Past (15 minutes).
  • When the minute hand points to 6, it is Half Past (30 minutes).
  • When the minute hand points to 9, it is Quarter To the next hour! (45 minutes).
Reading Digital Clocks:
📱 Reading Digital Clocks 📱

Numbers flashing on your phone and microwave!

1. What is a digital clock?

A digital clock displays time using numbers instead of hands. You read it from left to right! The number before the colon (:) tells you the hour. The number after the colon tells you the minutes!

2. What is a leading zero?

Digital clocks like to keep things neat, so they use a "leading zero" if a number is only one digit long. 07:05 means exactly seven hours and five minutes. (Do not confuse 07:05 with 07:50! Five minutes is very different from fifty minutes!).

3. Common Digital Times

  • 06:00 is exactly Six o'clock.
  • 09:15 is Quarter past nine (15 minutes past).
  • 02:30 is Half past two (30 minutes past).
  • 04:45 is Quarter to five (15 minutes before 5:00).
Hours, Minutes and Seconds:
⏱️ Hours, Minutes & Seconds ⏱️

Breaking down time from tiny ticks to long journeys!

1. The Three Units

  • Second (s): Super fast! A quick clap or a heartbeat.
  • Minute (min): Takes a little while! Brushing your teeth takes about 2 minutes.
  • Hour (h): A long time! A movie or a long car ride.

2. The Golden Rule of 60

Time doesn't use tens or hundreds; it uses the magic number 60!

To convert hours to minutes, multiply by 60! (2 hours × 60 = 120 minutes).

To convert minutes to seconds, multiply by 60! (3 minutes × 60 = 180 seconds).

3. Working Backwards

If you have 180 seconds and want to know how many minutes that is, divide by 60! (180 ÷ 60 = 3 minutes). If a timer says 125 seconds, that is exactly 2 minutes and 5 seconds!
☀️ A.M. vs. P.M. 🌙

Knowing the difference between breakfast and dinner time!

1. What do they mean?

Because our 12-hour clocks only go up to 12, the numbers have to repeat twice a day! We use A.M. and P.M. to tell them apart.

  • a.m.: (Ante Meridiem). This means morning time! It runs from midnight until just before lunch.
  • p.m.: (Post Meridiem). This means afternoon and evening! It runs from lunch all the way until you go to sleep at midnight.

2. Noon vs. Midnight

These two are the easiest to mix up! 12:00 P.M. is Noon (Midday when the sun is highest). 12:00 A.M. is Midnight (when you are fast asleep and a brand new day begins on the calendar!).
12-hour and 24-hour time:
🛫 24-Hour Time 🛫

The clock used by trains, planes, and the military!

1. The 24-Hour Clock

The 24-hour clock doesn't use a.m. or p.m. Instead, it just keeps counting up from 00 to 23! It is used for plane tickets and train schedules so nobody gets confused and misses their ride.

2. Converting P.M. to 24-Hour Time

For morning times (a.m.), the numbers are exactly the same! 8:15 a.m. is just written as 08:15.

But for afternoon and evening times (p.m.), you must ADD 12 to the hour! 1:00 p.m. becomes 13:00. 4:30 p.m. becomes 16:30. 9:45 p.m. becomes 21:45!

3. Midnight

Midnight is the start of a brand new day, so the clock resets to zero! 12:00 a.m. is written as 00:00.
Converting Units of Time:
📅 The Calendar Conversions 📅

From seconds to years, how time builds up!

1. Bigger Time Units

We already know that 60 seconds make a minute, and 60 minutes make an hour. But time keeps getting bigger!

  • 24 Hours = 1 Day. (To find how many hours are in 3 days, multiply 3 × 24 = 72 hours).
  • 7 Days = 1 Week. (To find how many days are in 4 weeks, multiply 4 × 7 = 28 days).
  • 12 Months = 1 Year.

2. Mixed Units

Sometimes time is mixed, like "2 hours and 30 minutes". To convert that entirely into minutes, do the big unit first! 2 hours × 60 = 120 minutes. Then add the remaining 30 minutes! 120 + 30 = 150 minutes total!
Calculating Elapsed Time:
⏳ Elapsed Time ⏳

Figuring out exactly how long something takes!

1. What is elapsed time?

Elapsed time is the amount of time that passes between a start time and an end time. If a soccer game starts at 3:00 p.m. and ends at 5:00 p.m., the elapsed time is 2 hours!

2. The Counting Forward Method

If a movie starts at 2:40 p.m. and ends at 4:10 p.m., you should break it into jumps to make it easy!

  • Jump 1: 2:40 p.m. up to 3:00 p.m. is 20 minutes.
  • Jump 2: 3:00 p.m. up to 4:00 p.m. is 1 hour.
  • Jump 3: 4:00 p.m. up to 4:10 p.m. is 10 minutes.

Now add your jumps together: 1 hour + 20 mins + 10 mins = 1 hour and 30 minutes!
Days, Weeks, Months and Years:
📅 The Julian Calendar 📅

Organizing our lives into months and years!

1. The 12 Months

A year has 12 months, but they don't all have the same number of days! Most months have 30 or 31 days. (September, April, June, and November have 30!). February is the shortest month with only 28 days.

2. What is a Leap Year?

Every four years, we add one extra day to the calendar to keep it perfectly aligned with the Earth spinning around the Sun! That extra day goes to February (giving it 29 days). A Leap Year has 366 days instead of the normal 365.

3. Calendar Math

If you need to know how many days are in 2 years, just add 365 + 365 = 730 days!
Reading Calendars:
📆 Reading a Calendar 📆

Navigating the rows and columns of the month!

1. Columns and Rows

A monthly calendar has 7 columns for the days of the week. If you look at a date (like Monday the 1st), the date directly underneath it in the same column will ALWAYS be exactly 7 days later (Monday the 8th)!

2. Counting Elapsed Days

If a party starts on Monday the 8th and your next event is Thursday the 11th, how many days pass?

  • Tuesday the 9th is 1 day.
  • Wednesday the 10th is 2 days.
  • Thursday the 11th is 3 days.

The elapsed time is 3 days! (Be careful: If a question asks how many dates are "included" from the 8th to the 11th, you must count all four dates: 8, 9, 10, 11).
Timetables and Schedules:
🚌 Timetables 🚌

Making sure you never miss the bus!

1. What is a timetable?

A timetable is a chart that shows exactly when activities or journeys are planned to happen (like school subjects or bus stops). It shows Departure times (when you leave) and Arrival times (when you get there).

2. Arriving Early

If your soccer game starts at 4:00 p.m., but your coach says to arrive 15 minutes early, you have to count backwards! 5 minutes early is 3:55, 10 minutes early is 3:50, and 15 minutes early is 3:45 p.m.!
Time Word Problems:
🕵️‍♂️ Time Mysteries 🕵️‍♀️

Solving real-world puzzles using the clock!

1. Finding the Finish Time

If a lesson begins at 11:25 a.m. and lasts 40 minutes, when does it finish? You have to add! Add 35 minutes to reach exactly 12:00 noon. Then add the remaining 5 minutes. It finishes at 12:05 p.m.! (Remember, 11:45 plus 30 minutes does NOT equal 11:75, it rolls over into the next hour!).

2. Crossing Midnight

If a flight leaves at 10:30 p.m. and lands at 1:00 a.m. the next day, how long was the flight?

  • 10:30 p.m. to midnight is 1 hour and 30 minutes.
  • Midnight to 1:00 a.m. is 1 hour.

The total flight time is 2 hours and 30 minutes!
